primary.title: Elements
primary.author: Euclid
primary.rationale: Euclid's seminal work on geometry, considered one of the most influential works in the history of mathematics. It has been translated and published numerous times.

secondary.title: Euclid's Elements
secondary.author: Thomas L. Heath
secondary.rationale: While published before 1976, Heath's edition and commentary on Euclid's Elements is considered the definitive scholarly English translation and analysis, often referenced in later works. It is widely available.

secondary.title: The Thirteen Books of Euclid's Elements
secondary.author: Euclid
secondary.rationale: This is a foundational English translation and commentary by Thomas L. Heath, essential for any serious study of Euclid's work. It is a primary source in translation but often treated as a secondary scholarly resource due to its extensive commentary.

secondary.title: Euclid
secondary.author: Reviel Netz
secondary.rationale: A scholarly analysis of Euclid's life and work, focusing on the historical context and reception of his mathematical texts.

suggestions.notes: Euclid's primary contribution is 'Elements', which exists in many translations and editions. Secondary sources often focus on the analysis and historical context of 'Elements'.
